title: Mundari: language, identity and living knowledge
author: Mundari Samaj Editorial Desk
excerpt: An introduction to the language and the importance of documenting it with care, context and community voices.

body.text: Mundari is a language of the Munda communities, with speakers across parts of eastern and central India and beyond. Like every living language, it carries ways of describing relationships, land, work, memory and the world.
A language lives through its speakers

Language preservation is not only about recording words. It also means supporting everyday use, intergenerational learning, songs, oral histories, local expressions and the many contexts in which people communicate.

Spelling, pronunciation and usage can vary by region and speaker. A responsible language resource should record who shared a word, where it is used, how it is pronounced and whether a native-speaker review has taken place.

title: Why oral histories matter
author: Mundari Samaj Editorial Desk
excerpt: Family memories and community accounts can preserve details that formal archives may not contain.

body.text: An oral history is a recorded account of a person's memories and experiences. It can help future generations understand how people remember places, livelihoods, celebrations, change and community life.
Explain how a recording may be used, ask what should remain private, and allow the speaker to pause or withdraw permission. Do not assume every story is intended for public sharing.

title: Building a respectful community archive
author: Mundari Samaj Editorial Desk
excerpt: A practical guide to credit, consent and context when sharing photographs, documents and cultural knowledge.

body.text: A community archive can bring together photographs, documents, recordings and stories that help people explore their heritage. The value of an archive depends on how material was collected and described.
Before publishing a photograph, recording or document, confirm who owns it and whether the project has permission to display it. Credit the creator or contributor in the way they request.
